arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Douglas Laycock argued the church controls its own clergy selection.
He stated government does not set criteria for church officers.
The government argued religious freedom must accommodate public welfare.
Justice Scalia noted it is not government business to judge church interests.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests whether the First Amendment blocks courts from applying employment laws to church staff. The church argues religious freedom requires total control over its clergy. The government argues anti-discrimination laws protect workers in all sectors.
